title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Non-Timber Forest Products"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Non-timber forest products cover what forests yield other than wood. The account values them as
the non-wood forest product (NWFP) value per hectare times each country's FAO total forest. The
base year is 2019 and the price convention recorded in `es_config.csv` is
`value per hectare of total forest`. No share is taken out for human inputs (λ = 1), as the
write-up states: the per-hectare value already embeds it.

## Source

The rate is IUCN's NWFP value per hectare per country, the series CWoN 2024 publishes
(`nontimber_price_iucn_edited.csv`, equal to IUCN's 2019 series in all 232 countries it covers).
The source report, *Global Assessment of the Economic Value of Non-Wood Forest Ecosystem
Services* (World Bank P178446), predicts the value on the NWFP service area, averages it over each
country's total forest (PDF page 61, printed 53) and multiplies by FAO total forest (PDF page 63,
printed 55). CWoN's code does the same (`forest_nontimber.do` line 340), and its comment calls
the published value an average "per hectare of forest, by country" (`tornqvist_index_master.do`
line 156). The account follows that construction.

The write-up is `Non-Timber Forest Product Provision.docx` in the shared folder of current
write-ups (version of 29 October 2026). The registered author code is `Observarun/geo-ntfp` at
`928dc21`, a fork of `martaszk/geo_ntfp`. It multiplies the rate by accessible forest, which the
account reports as a comparison table.

## Quantity

FAO total forest per country in 2019, in hectares, written by `fao_forest`:

- FAO FRA 2020 for every country, interpolated linearly between 2015 and 2020, which is CWoN's
  rule (`forest_timber_depletion.do` line 518). FRA 2020 reports thousand hectares, so the value is
  multiplied by 1,000 (236 countries).
- A country FRA 2020 cannot give stays missing (14 countries). Nothing is filled from the land
  cover or from CWoN, and nothing is set to zero that FRA does not report as zero.

The area CWoN publishes (`forest_nontimber_total_area.xlsx`, 151 countries in 2019) is the area
its own NWFP value multiplies. `cwon_forest` writes it for the comparison below, and the account's
value does not read it. It equals FRA 2020 interpolated in 145 of the 151, 115 bit for bit and 30
to within a billionth. The other six are from FRA 2010, as the next section sets out.

Both files are copied unchanged from the CWoN 2024 reproducibility package (FR_WLD_2024_195) into
`base_data/global_invest/ntfp/cwon_2024_forest_area/`, with their SHA-256 and provenance.
`es_parameters.csv` names the package ZIP and the member for each, so
`utilities.download_missing_inputs` fetches either where it is not staged.

## Six areas from FRA 2010

CWoN's code ranks FRA 2020 first. It reads FRA 2010 for 1970 to 2010, overwrites every year FRA
2020 reports (`forest_timber_depletion.do` line 511), then interpolates and extrapolates the rest
(line 518). Yet for BOL, CIV, CZE, GBR, MKD and SWZ the published 2019 area is FRA 2010's 2005 to
2010 trend extrapolated to 2019, to the hectare, not FRA 2020.

The cause is in how FRA 2020 rows get a country code. The block keeps only the `name` column
(line 440) and maps by hand the names its lookup cannot read (lines 450 to 464), testing a variable
`country`. With no such variable, Stata reads `country` as an abbreviation of `countrycode`, which
is empty for exactly these rows, so no mapping applies. The rows without a code are dropped (line
469), and these countries keep only their FRA 2010 years. Across CWoN's whole 2019 series, 199 of
209 areas are FRA 2020 and 10 are FRA 2010 extrapolated. The 10 are every published country whose
FRA 2020 name is mapped by hand (the six, CPV and VEN) and two names the code never maps (MAF and
MNP). The hand mappings that name a form FRA 2020 does not use (ETH, SDN, TUR, TZA) change
nothing, since the lookup reads FRA 2020's own names for these four, and they stay on FRA 2020.

The account values these six on FRA 2020, like every other country, because FRA 2020 is the
vintage CWoN's code ranks first and their FRA 2010 areas come from a matching fault. The
previous rule, CWoN's published area where CWoN has one and FRA 2020 elsewhere, valued the same
223 countries at \$31,809,823,610.73, which is \$71,924,158.11 more than the account. CWoN's
published areas alone cover 149 of them, at \$30,281,055,011.16 against the account's
\$30,209,130,853.06 there. The whole difference is in the six:

| Country | CWoN area (ha) | FRA 2020 (ha) | Account minus CWoN area (USD) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CIV | 10,399,400 | 2,949,598 | −58,314,162.51 |
| BOL | 54,427,600 | 51,072,452 | −19,132,707.02 |
| SWZ | 602,600 | 496,348 | −712,907.61 |
| MKD | 1,039,400 | 1,000,072 | −155,333.86 |
| CZE | 2,675,000 | 2,675,350 | +6,243.71 |
| GBR | 2,945,800 | 3,183,000 | +6,384,709.19 |

The other 145 CWoN areas move the total by a hundred-millionth of a dollar.

## Price

The rate at the GEP base year from `nontimber_price_iucn_edited.csv`, in current USD, unadjusted.

## Valuation

`gep_calculation` joins the rate onto the FAO area by country label and multiplies:

$$
\text{NTFP GEP} = \text{FAO total forest (ha)} \times \text{NWFP value (USD/ha)}
$$

A missing area or rate gives a missing value, and a zero of either gives zero.

## Alternatives

Each is its own task and table, run by the same tree with no switch, and none is the account's
value.

- `divide_by_five_sensitivity` writes `gep_by_country_divide_by_five.csv`. It divides the rate by
  five for the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mozambique and the Central African Republic, as
  CWoN's code does at `forest_nontimber.do` line 305 with no reason given. The countries and the
  divisor are `ntfp_divide_by_five_labels` and `ntfp_divide_by_five_divisor` in `es_parameters.csv`.
- `cwon_forest` and `cwon_forest_comparison` write `cwon_forest_ha_by_country.csv` and
  `gep_by_country_cwon_forest.csv`, the rate times the area CWoN publishes, for the 149 countries
  CWoN values that carry a rate. It reproduces CWoN's own value (below).
- `esa_forest` and `esa_forest_sensitivity` write `esa_forest_ha_by_country.csv` and
  `gep_by_country_esa_forest.csv`. They value all mapped ESA forest, classes 50 to 90 with the NDVI
  screen, on the account grid, wherever a road or river reaches it or not. The comparison of the
  area source with the reach rests on this table.
- `accessible_forest` and `accessible_forest_valuation` write `accessible_forest_ha_by_country.csv`
  and `gep_by_country_accessible_forest.csv`, the earlier valuation, kept for comparison.

The ESA and accessible forest tasks read global rasters on the account grid. Forest is ESA CCI 2019 land cover,
classes 50 to 90 inclusive, kept where the 2015 to 2019 mean NDVI (MODIS MOD13Q1) is at least
0.20. A cell with no NDVI is dropped, and the floor is compared in the raster's own integers. Cell
hectares come from `ha_per_cell_10sec.tif`, and a cell belongs to the country whose boundary covers
its centre. Accessible means within 10 km of a road (GRIP4, Meijer et al. 2018, all 25,758,453
lines, `grip4_global_roads.gpkg`) or a river (Natural Earth 10 m centre lines), measured in metres
at each latitude up to 84 degrees. Both tasks run on the cluster and skip once their table exists.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `ntfp` service: `ntfp_value_per_ha_path` and
`ntfp_fra_forest_input_path` for the account's value, `ntfp_cwon_forest_area_input_path` for the
comparison, `ntfp_divide_by_five_labels` and `ntfp_divide_by_five_divisor` for that sensitivity,
and `ntfp_roads_vector_path`, `ntfp_rivers_path` and `ntfp_ndvi_mean_path` for the forest rasters.
Each carries its source in a `_source` or `_source_note` row. The two FAO inputs also carry a
`_source_url` and `_source_archive_member`. The rate table is not in the CWoN package, and its note
names the public file whose values it carries, `Input_data/nontimber_ecosystem_services_iucn.csv`
of `martaszk/geo_ntfp`, equal in all 6,032 cells. The land cover is the `es_config.csv` row's
`gep_lulc_input_path`, `lulc/esa/lulc_esa_2019.tif`.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the
r250 identifiers and attributes, `fao_forest_ha`, `fao_forest_source`, `nwfp_value_per_ha`,
`ntfp_gep` and `year`.

## Coverage

One row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in 2019 USD.
\$31,737,899,452.62 over 223 valued countries, 211 positive and 12 zero, on 4.06 billion FAO
hectares.

- 12 are zero. Nine have a zero rate in the published rate table (AIA, BMU, COK, FSM, GRL, KIR,
  MYT, SJM, SPM), so their value is zero for any area, and FAO reports zero forest in three (FLK,
  GIB, QAT).
- 18 are missing because the rate table has no row for them (ATA, BLM, BVT, CCK, ESH, HMD, IOT,
  KWT, MAF, MCO, MDV, MHL, MSR, NRU, PCN, TKL, TUV, VAT).
- 9 carry a rate and no FAO area. FRA 2020 counts Åland under Finland and Hong Kong and Macao under
  China (FRA 2020 main report, page 5). Serbia's series includes Kosovo, whose 461 thousand
  hectares are part of the 2010 total in FRA 2010's Serbia report, the total FRA 2020 repeats. The
  forest of ALA, HKG, MAC and XKX therefore enters the account in FIN, CHN and SRB, at those
  countries' rates. TWN, CXR, ATF, SGS and UMI are outside FRA 2020. SGS and UMI have a zero rate
  in the published table.

Against the earlier valuation, 7 positive values become missing (TWN \$63.87M, XKX \$2.32M, ALA
\$1.34M, HKG \$1.31M, CXR \$0.39M, MAC and ATF), 3 become zero (FLK, GIB, QAT), 3 zeros become
positive because FAO reports forest where no ESA forest is accessible (EGY, MLT, MRT), and SGS and
UMI go from zero to missing.

## Reproduction

The comparison table, the rate times CWoN's own areas, gives \$30,281,055,011.16 on the 149
countries CWoN values in 2019. It equals CWoN's published value to within \$0.40 in 146 of them
and is five times it in COD, MOZ and CAF, whose rate CWoN divides by five and the account does
not. With the divide-by-five applied to it, the total is \$28,877,638,160.27, against CWoN's
published \$28,877,638,160.26, at most \$0.40 apart in any country. The rate file prints IUCN's
float32 values to 10 significant digits, and with the float32 values the largest gap is a
millionth of a dollar. On the account's FRA 2020 areas, the divide-by-five table equals CWoN's
published value to within \$0.40 in 143 of the 149 and differs in the six areas CWoN took from FRA
2010.

## Alternatives, measured

| USD 2019 | All valued countries | 149 countries CWoN values |
|---|---:|---:|
| Account, FAO FRA 2020 total forest | 31,737,899,452.62 (223) | 30,209,130,853.06 |
| CWoN's published forest area | 30,281,055,011.16 (149) | 30,281,055,011.16 |
| Divide-by-five on FAO forest | 30,334,482,601.73 (223) | 28,805,714,002.16 |
| All mapped ESA forest | 28,698,224,200.33 (232) | 27,198,510,413.08 |
| Accessible ESA forest, earlier valuation | 20,491,261,549.18 (232) | 19,435,175,714.64 |

On the 149 countries, accessibility accounts for \$7.76bn of the \$10.77bn between the last row and
the first, and the area source, ESA forest against FAO statistics, for \$3.01bn. ESA forest exceeds
FAO forest in 55 of the 149.

## Method constants

- `NTFP_ACCESS_BUFFER_M = 10_000`, the accessibility reach around roads and rivers.
- `ESA_FOREST_CLASS_MIN = 50` and `ESA_FOREST_CLASS_MAX = 90`, the inclusive forest class range.
- `NDVI_MIN_THRESHOLD = 0.20`, the vegetation floor.

## What is open

- The divide-by-five. No reason for it is stated in CWoN's code, the source report, the package
  documents or the CWoN 2024 report. It stays a separate sensitivity until one is found.
- Taiwan. FRA 2020 does not cover it, and the national inventory completed in 2015 reports 2.197
  million hectares. The account leaves it missing.
